slice.question: Do the documented public GitHub artifact-attestation or Sigstore/Rekor retrieval surfaces provide a repository-identity plus release-predicate/tag lookup, or a deterministic deletion-surviving lookup key derivable from immutable-release metadata without pre-retaining UUID, log index, subject digest, artifact hash, public key, or other external state?

sources.title: REST API endpoints for artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: Organization attestation-repository listing can filter by predicate_type=release but returns repository identities, while attestation listing itself is keyed by subject_digest. The documented repository and user variants are likewise keyed by subject digest; predicate_type is a filter, not a repository-plus-tag discovery key.

sources.title: Immutable releases - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: An immutable release automatically generates a release attestation containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets. Those fields are inside the attestation; the documentation does not define a subject digest or Rekor lookup identifier deterministically computable from repository identity plus a deleted release tag alone.

sources.title: Managing the lifecycle of artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: GitHub's UI supports subject-name and predicate filtering, but the REST management surface remains subject-digest keyed; the page also states that after an attestation is deleted it can no longer be found on GitHub. This does not establish a public post-release-deletion repository-plus-tag lookup.

sources.title: CLI - Sigstore
sources.observed: Rekor get is documented by log index or UUID. Rekor search is documented by artifact, public key, or SHA hash. No repository identity, GitHub release predicate, or release-tag query is documented.

sources.title: Threat Model - Sigstore
sources.observed: Sigstore describes publishing artifact hash, signature, and certificate to the transparency log and notes identity monitoring for some hashedrekord entries, but this documentation does not establish a release-tag-indexed lookup for GitHub automatic release attestations.

reasoning: The best documented GitHub REST path can identify repositories that have release-predicate attestations, but retrieving the attestations themselves requires a subject digest; repository identity plus release tag is not a documented lookup key.

The automatic release attestation contains tag, commit SHA, and assets only after the attestation is retrieved. Using those fields to derive its own lookup identifier is therefore circular unless some digest or identifier was retained separately.

The best documented Rekor paths require UUID/log index for direct retrieval or artifact/public-key/SHA for search. None is shown derivable solely from surviving repository identity plus a deleted release tag.

Therefore the public transparency layer remains useful for independent retention but does not yet remove the residual deletion-surviving discovery-key dependency. The monotonic rollback-witness child remains unresolved.
